questions.question_text: An organization is developing a generative AI application that will be used across multiple teams. Which two measures should the organization implement to ensure governance and compliance while maintaining transparency in model outputs? (Select TWO)
options: A. AWS CodePipeline for continuous integration and deployment of models
B. AWS S3 for storing training data, ensuring version control and access logs
C. AWS GuardDuty for monitoring and detecting potential security threats to the AI application
D. AWS SageMaker Model Monitor for tracking and validating model performance and bias
E. AWS Config for defining and enforcing governance policies across all AWS services
questions.explanation:
A. AWS CodePipeline is a continuous integration and delivery service, which is not directly related to governance or compliance measures in the context of AI model outputs.

B. AWS S3 provides storage with version control and access logs, ensuring that data used for training models is properly managed and auditable, aligning with governance and compliance requirements.

C. AWS GuardDuty is a security service for monitoring and detecting threats to your AWS environment, which does not directly address the specific needs of AI model outputs or transparency.

D. AWS SageMaker Model Monitor helps track and validate model performance and bias, ensuring that models are transparent and explainable, which aligns with governance and compliance requirements in the context of AI applications.

E. AWS Config is a service for defining and enforcing governance policies across all AWS services, but it does not directly address the specific needs of AI model outputs or transparency.

questions.question_text: An e-commerce company wants to implement a recommendation system that can suggest products based on customer browsing history. The system should be scalable, cost-effective, and capable of handling both online and offline data. Which two AWS services would best meet these requirements? (Select TWO)
options: A. Amazon SageMaker
B. Amazon Redshift
C. Amazon Kinesis
D. Amazon DynamoDB
E. AWS Glue
questions.explanation:
A. Amazon SageMaker: Amazon SageMaker is a fully managed service that provides developers and data scientists with the ability to build, train, and deploy machine learning models quickly. It supports both online and offline data processing and can scale automatically based on demand, making it cost-effective for large-scale applications like recommendation systems.

B. NOT RELEVANT: Amazon Redshift is a fully managed data warehouse service that provides fast, parallel query performance for petabyte-scale data sets. While useful for analytics, it is not specifically designed for real-time or online recommendation systems and does not meet the scalability requirements mentioned in the scenario.

C. Amazon Kinesis: Amazon Kinesis can process and analyze streaming data in real time, which is suitable for handling customer browsing history data as part of a recommendation system. It supports both online and offline processing and can scale automatically to handle varying loads.

D. NOT RELEVANT: Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database service that provides fast and predictable performance with seamless scalability. While it could be used in the backend, it does not directly support real-time recommendation systems or streaming data processing as required by the scenario.

E. AWS Glue: AWS Glue is a fully managed extract, transform, load (ETL) service for preparing data to be analyzed and stored in data lakes. It is primarily used for data integration tasks and does not provide real-time capabilities or machine learning services that are necessary for building recommendation systems.

Option D, while useful for recommendation systems, does not directly address the need to train a model from historical and real-time data.

They want to ensure the model's outputs are secure, compliant, and can be audited for accuracy. Which two strategies should they implement according to AWS best practices? (Select TWO)
options: A. Deploy the AI model in a VPC with security groups to restrict access.
B. Use Amazon SageMaker to train the model but ignore all built-in logging features.
C. Configure AWS Config rules for continuous compliance checks of the AI environment.

B. Use Amazon SageMaker to train the model but ignore all built-in logging features - This is incorrect as ignoring built-in logging features would violate the best practice of establishing comprehensive audit logging capabilities for monitoring and auditing model outputs.

C. Configure AWS Config rules for continuous compliance checks of the AI environment - While this is a good practice, it is not specifically mentioned in the provided sources as being critical for generative AI applications compared to other options.

D. Implement Amazon GuardDuty to monitor network traffic and detect potential threats - This is more relevant for general network security and threat detection rather than specific auditing of model outputs, making it a less direct fit for the scenario.

E. Enable Amazon CloudWatch logs for detailed monitoring and auditing of the AI model's outputs - This aligns with AWS best practices as it ensures detailed monitoring and auditing capabilities are in place to track and verify model outputs, which is critical for compliance and security.

Custom authentication layers (Option B) can be complex and may introduce additional security risks if not implemented correctly. Direct Jupyter notebook use from S3 buckets (Option D) is convenient but does not offer the necessary network isolation or logging capabilities.

questions.question_text: An organization is developing a generative AI application that will be deployed across multiple teams. To ensure the security and compliance of this application, which two measures should the organization implement? (Select TWO)
options: A. AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies to control access to model endpoints
B. Amazon S3 for storing all AI training data without encryption
C. AWS CloudTrail to monitor API calls related to AI models
D. Amazon SageMaker endpoint configurations with network isolation using VPCs
E. AWS Config to set up compliance checks but not enable any enforcement actions
questions.explanation:
A. CORRECT - IAM policies are crucial for controlling access to AI model endpoints, ensuring that only authorized users and services can interact with the models. This aligns with governance and compliance requirements.

B. INCORRECT - Storing data without encryption is not compliant with AWS best practices, especially when dealing with sensitive information in generative AI applications. AWS recommends encrypting all data at rest using KMS keys.

C. CORRECT - AWS CloudTrail can be used to monitor API calls related to AI models, which helps in identifying any unauthorized access or usage patterns. This is part of the risk management discipline.

D. CORRECT - Configuring endpoints with network isolation using VPCs ensures that the AI models are only accessible within a trusted environment, reducing the risk of data breaches and ensuring compliance with security policies.

E. INCORRECT - While AWS Config can be used to set up compliance checks, it does not enforce any actions by default. Enforcing actions is necessary for effective governance, and simply setting up checks without enforcement would leave the organization vulnerable.
